bibl.title: The Ten Articles of William I: French translation

listBibl.bibl: Felix Liebermann, Die Gesetze der Angelsachsen, vol. 1 (Halle: Niemeyer, 1903), p. 489

A semi-literal English rendering of the Anglo-Norman French text, created for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model made by Anthropic. It is a crib to help the reader with the French, and should not be treated as a separate translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: Wl art Frz 8.3
div.ab: e si il a la quarte feis ne venent, seit rendu de lur chatel ce ke fut chalengé, ke li Engleis apelent chapgield; e ensurketut la forfeture.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 489 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: and if they do not come the fourth time, let what was claimed be paid from their chattels, which the English call chapgield (payment of the value); and over and above that the forfeiture.
